video.title: The Magic of Single-Foot Forehand Training

classification.reason: The coach presents and analyzes a single-foot probing drill to correct foot placement, weight transfer, and visual tracking on the forehand.

problem.title_as_question: Why should you practice forehand probing on one foot, and how does it fix foot positioning and weight transfer?
problem.definition: Players often fail to run deep enough and get their loading foot behind the ball, preventing proper weight transfer and causing them to reach or miss when misjudging ball distance.
prerequisites: loading on the outside foot on the forehand
hitting forehands moving into the corner

symptoms.description: Reaching with the arm and curling the ball around instead of pressing through with body weight.
Absence of body weight transfer through the court toward the target.
Upper body leaning excessively or falling forward to adjust for incorrect ball spacing.
Shot feels poor or results in outright misses when ball position is sub-optimal.

causes.statement: The loading foot does not get positioned behind the ball and deep enough into the corner.
Deficient probing skill and visual tracking to align body spacing with the incoming ball.
Attempting to take the exact same rigid swing regardless of being in the wrong spot.

angles.summary: The loading foot must position behind the ball and deep in the corner to enable pushing through the court and transferring body weight.
Alexa consistently probes into the optimal spot with minimal compensation, whereas the coach's imperfect probing requires upper body leaning to save the shot.
Players wrongly try to take the identical swing on every ball and miss poorly probed shots instead of watching the ball and adjusting with the body.
Reaching around the ball without proper foot loading may get the ball over the net but will never feel good.

solutions.summary: Hop and probe the ball on one foot only, forcing the player to load deep behind the ball and press back through the court.
solutions.external_goal: press the foot back towards the court

solutions.summary: Look at the ball and swing through the ball you see, using bodily adjustments to maintain contact rather than rigidly taking a pre-set swing.
solutions.external_goal: look at the ball and swing through the ball
